info.title: Crypto Idea API
info.description:
Complete HTTP surface of the Crypto Idea backend (Firebase Cloud Functions v1 + Firestore security rules).

Three kinds of endpoint are documented:

1. **Public REST** (`/api/*`) — the `api` HTTP function. No authentication. Serves cached CoinGecko market data to the landing DCA calculator and the app, plus the public app config and the landing email-capture form. In production these are also reachable at `https://<your-domain>/api/*` via a Firebase Hosting rewrite (`firebase.json`).

2. **Callable functions** — Firebase `onCall` functions. The Firebase SDK POSTs `{"data": <input>}` and receives `{"result": <output>}`; on error it returns a non-2xx status with `{"error": {"message", "status", "details"}}`. Every callable verifies the caller's Firebase ID token server-side and acts on `context.auth.uid` — never a uid taken from the request body (no IDOR by design). **Admin** callables additionally require the verified `{admin:true}` custom claim, which now also carries a role: `manager` (account management, granted by an owner from the Admin access tab) or `owner` (minted ONLY by `functions/scripts/set-admin.js --role=owner`). The owner-only callables (`getAdminConfig`, `saveConfig`, `setManagerRole`) additionally require a password re-auth within the last ~600s (step-up).

3. **PayPal webhook** (`/paypalWebhook`) — the only inbound write not gated by a Firebase user login; it is authenticated instead by PayPal's webhook signature (documented as the `PayPalWebhookSignature` scheme). Every event is cryptographically verified against PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API before it is trusted.

Security model summary: Firestore rules are the authorization boundary (owner-only data, closed-shape user doc, users cannot write their own `tier`/`subscription`/`premiumLimits`/`deleted`). Secrets (CoinGecko / PayPal / SMTP / AI provider keys) live only in the server-side locked `config/app` Firestore doc or environment variables; they are never returned to a client and never shipped in the browser bundle.

servers.description: Production — Cloud Functions base (replace YOUR_PROJECT at go-live). REST is also served at https://<your-domain>/api/* via the Hosting rewrite. Local development uses the Firebase emulator at localhost:5001/<project>/us-central1 (localhost-only, no TLS — never network-exposed); it is intentionally not listed as a server URL here so the documented contract stays HTTPS-only. See README.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: Admin-only operations. Require the verified {admin:true} custom claim in one of two roles: `manager` (read + account management) or `owner` (Settings, manager grants, permanent erasure — plus a step-up password re-auth). Owners are protected by IDENTITY: they can never be deleted, trashed, demoted or self-deleted, and a manager may not act on an owner at all; the MIN_ADMINS count is only a secondary floor. firestore.rules matches — any admin may READ users, but the blanket update/delete branches are owner-only. Kept in the PRIVATE repo.

post.description: The only public unauthenticated write. Emails the captured address to the site owner over SMTP (provider-agnostic — configured in admin Settings; no provider is hardcoded and no key reaches the client). Protected by a strict per-IP budget (5/min), a honeypot field, and (at go-live) App Check/reCAPTCHA.

post.summary: Start a PayPal subscription checkout for the signed-in user
post.description: Callable. Creates a PayPal subscription for `context.auth.uid` and returns the approval URL. The PayPal plan is selected server-side from the requested tier × billing cycle (H6: pro/premium × monthly/yearly), so a yearly buyer is charged the yearly plan. Guards against re-buying the current tier and against duplicate submissions (60s per-uid cooldown).

200.description: Approval URL to redirect the user to.

401.description: Not signed in.

500.description: internal / failed-precondition (already on this plan, plan not configured).

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Schedule a future-start Pro downgrade for a Premium user (Plan B PR-C2)
post.description: Callable. A Premium user schedules a REAL future-start PayPal Pro subscription that first-charges when Premium ends (start_time == the premium period end), so the account lands directly on Pro with a real payment — no early tier drop, no double-charge. Server-authoritative + fail-closed: paused by the paidPlansEnabled master switch (which takes precedence over the checkout kill-switch); refuses a non-premium or already-scheduled caller; 60s per-uid cooldown. Acts on context.auth.uid only. Returns the PayPal approval URL (the client redirects); the schedule is PENDING until the scheduled sub's ACTIVATED webhook confirms payment.

200.description: Approval URL to redirect the user to (null in the DEV/emulator branch).

400.description: invalid-argument (unknown field) / failed-precondition (paused, checkout unavailable, not premium, already scheduled, plan not configured).

401.description: Not signed in.

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Seamless future-start Premium re-subscribe for a cancelled-Premium user (Plan B PR-C3b-server)
post.description: Callable. A CANCELLED-Premium user schedules a REAL future-start PayPal Premium subscription that first-charges when the current period ends, so Premium continues seamlessly with a real payment — no early tier drop, no double-charge. Shares one engine with scheduleProDowngrade; the marker is tier-carrying (subscription.scheduledNext.tier == "premium"). Server-authoritative + fail-closed: paused by the paidPlansEnabled master switch (which takes precedence over the checkout kill-switch); refuses a non-premium, a non-cancelled premium, or a caller who still has a pending scheduledNext downgrade (founder rule: re-subscribe requires a prior "Keep my plan" — the scheduled downgrade is NOT auto-cancelled); 60s per-uid cooldown. Acts on context.auth.uid only. Returns the PayPal approval URL (the client redirects); the schedule is PENDING until the scheduled sub's ACTIVATED webhook confirms payment.

200.description: Approval URL to redirect the user to (null in the DEV/emulator branch).

400.description: invalid-argument (unknown field) / failed-precondition (paused, checkout unavailable, not a cancelled premium, a scheduled downgrade is still pending, plan not configured).

401.description: Not signed in.

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Wave-B AI research proxy — ask about your own holdings (Plan B PR-E2)
post.description: Callable. A signed-in user asks a question about THEIR OWN portfolio. The server builds a safety allowlist from the caller's own coin docs, generates via the configured generation model, and runs the fail-closed validate-output.js naming/advice/price wall plus the configured judge model on every candidate BEFORE any text reaches the client — so it NEVER returns financial advice, buy/sell/hold recommendations, price targets, allocation percentages or aggregate scores. Meters the actual token cost into the app-wide monthly aiBudget ledger. Fail-closed gate order: auth → question validation (non-blank, ≤500) + deny-by-default keys → aiResearch kill-switch (fresh config) → AI provider key + models present → per-uid daily budget → app-wide monthly $-cap. Acts on context.auth.uid only (no IDOR). Returns { answer, fellBack } — a fail-closed fallback is answer:"" / fellBack:true.

200.description: The answer (empty string on a fail-closed fallback) and whether it fell back.

400.description: invalid-argument (blank/non-string/too-long question, or an unknown field) / failed-precondition (aiResearch kill-switch off, or no AI provider key/models configured).

401.description: Not signed in.

429.description: resource-exhausted — the per-uid daily budget is exhausted, or the app-wide monthly $-cap has been reached.

503.description: unavailable — the monthly AI budget ledger could not be read (fail-closed refusal).

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.description: Callable, owner-only, and only with a password re-auth within the last ~600s. Grants or revokes the MANAGER role on another user by email; revoking clears the claim entirely and revokes the target's refresh tokens. Owner targets are refused in both directions (owners can only be minted by `functions/scripts/set-admin.js --role=owner`), as is the caller's own account. Replaces the removed `setAdminClaim`, which any admin could call to promote anyone.

post.summary: Read saved app config to pre-fill Settings (owner + Settings-password unlock)
post.description: Callable, owner-only, and behind the ADMIN-6 Settings-password unlock (`assertSettingsUnlocked`). Once a Settings password is set (`config/app.settingsAuth`), the caller must hold a live server-tracked unlock (`unlockSettings`, ~10 min) or the call fails `settings-locked`. Before any Settings password is set it falls back to the pre-ADMIN-6 step-up re-auth (recent password re-auth, `config/app.flags.stepUpReauth`, default on). Secrets are returned as boolean set-flags ONLY (e.g. `secretSet`, `providerKeySet`, and `settingsAuth.set`) — the secret values and the scrypt hash never leave the server.

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing, invalid, or expired ID token.

403.description: permission-denied — owners only. (A missing Settings-password unlock is reported as `failed-precondition` `settings-locked`, or `reauth-required` in the pre-password bootstrap.)

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Save app config / API keys (owner + Settings-password unlock)
post.description: Callable, owner-only, and behind the ADMIN-6 Settings-password unlock (`assertSettingsUnlocked`; a live `unlockSettings` within ~10 min once a Settings password is set, else the step-up re-auth bootstrap). Writes the locked `config/app` doc. A blank secret field keeps the saved value (`keep()` idiom); secrets are never echoed back. `settingsAuth` is NOT written here (owned by the set/change/reset callables) — the `{merge:true}` write preserves it. Clients can never read `config/app` (Firestore rules deny all access).

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing, invalid, or expired ID token.

403.description: permission-denied — owners only. (A missing Settings-password unlock is reported as `failed-precondition` `settings-locked`, or `reauth-required` in the pre-password bootstrap.)

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Set or change the owner-only Settings password (ADMIN-6)
post.description: Callable, owner-only. Sets the SECOND lock on the Settings screen (scrypt-hashed server-side; the plaintext is never stored or echoed). Setting the FIRST password requires a recent login re-auth (step-up); changing an existing one requires the current password or a live unlock. On success a fresh ~10-min unlock is granted. The event is audited (`setSettingsPassword`) but the password never is.

400.description: invalid-argument — the new password fails the strength floor (min 12 incl. upper+lower+number), or an unexpected field was sent.

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing, invalid, or expired ID token.

403.description: permission-denied — owners only; or (on a change) the current password is wrong and there is no live unlock; or (on a first set) the step-up re-auth is missing/stale (`reauth-required`).

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Unlock the Settings screen with the Settings password (ADMIN-6)
post.description: Callable, owner-only. Verifies the Settings password server-side (constant-time) and, on success, writes the short-lived server-tracked unlock (`settingsUnlock/{uid}`, ~10 min) that `getAdminConfig`/`saveConfig` require. Rate-limited per-uid/day to bound guessing; only FAILED attempts are audited (`settingsUnlockFailed`).

200.description: Unlocked — returns the unlock expiry (`until`, ms epoch).

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing, invalid, or expired ID token.

403.description: permission-denied — owners only, or the Settings password is incorrect.

429.description: resource-exhausted — too many unlock attempts today (per-uid daily cap).

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Email a Settings-password reset link (ADMIN-6 PR2)
post.description: Callable, owner-only. The recovery path for a forgotten Settings password. Generates a single-use token, stores it HASHED (only the sha256 is persisted; the raw token exists only in the email), and mails the link to the OWNER'S OWN verified address (`context.auth.token.email` — never a body value, so the reset can't be redirected). Fails `failed-precondition` when no Settings password is set to reset. Per-uid/day rate-limited. In dev / without SMTP configured the link is logged, not sent.

200.description: Reset link sent (or logged in dev).

400.description: invalid-argument — an unexpected field was sent; OR `failed-precondition` (no Settings password is set to reset). Both map to HTTP 400.

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing, invalid, or expired ID token.

429.description: resource-exhausted — too many reset requests today (per-uid daily cap).

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Complete a Settings-password reset with the emailed token (ADMIN-6 PR2)
post.description: Callable, owner-only. Redeems the single-use reset token (looked up by its hash) and installs the new password in one transaction, so a token can be redeemed at most once. The token is bound to the uid that requested it — a different owner can't redeem it. Fails `permission-denied` when the link is invalid, used, expired, or belongs to a different account; `invalid-argument` when the new password fails the strength floor (min 12 incl. upper+lower+number). On success a fresh ~10-min unlock is granted. The event is audited (`settingsPwResetCompleted`) but the password never is.

200.description: Reset — the new Settings password is active and the caller holds a fresh unlock.

400.description: invalid-argument — the new password fails the strength floor, or an unexpected field was sent.

401.description: Unauthenticated — missing, invalid, or expired ID token.

403.description: permission-denied — owners only, or the reset link is invalid / used / expired / belongs to a different account.

429.description: resource-exhausted — too many attempts today (per-uid daily cap).

default.description: Unexpected error — see the error body.

post.summary: Inbound PayPal subscription webhook (signature-verified)
post.description: PayPal posts subscription lifecycle events here. Every event is cryptographically verified against PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API BEFORE any DB write; unverified events are rejected. Idempotent (each event id processed once). Not called by clients.

FirebaseAuth.description: The signed-in user's Firebase ID token. The Firebase callable SDK sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>`; the function verifies it server-side and reads `context.auth.uid`. Admin operations additionally require the verified `{admin:true}` custom claim on that token, plus the `role` it carries (`owner` or `manager`). Owner-only operations may additionally require a step-up password re-auth within the last ~600s (`setManagerRole`, and the pre-password bootstrap for Settings — server flag `config/app.flags.stepUpReauth`, default on) OR the ADMIN-6 Settings-password unlock (`getAdminConfig`/`saveConfig`, once a Settings password is set). See each operation's description.

PayPalWebhookSignature.name: paypal-transmission-sig
PayPalWebhookSignature.description: PayPal's webhook transmission signature. Every event is cryptographically verified against PayPal's verify-webhook-signature API (using all five paypal-* headers) BEFORE it is trusted; unverified events are rejected. This documents that the webhook is authenticated (not public), even though it is not a bearer/OAuth flow.

CallableError.description: Firebase callable error envelope (returned with a non-2xx HTTP status).

status.description: Canonical status, e.g. UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, FAILED_PRECONDITION, NOT_FOUND, INTERNAL.

PricesResponse.description: Map of coin id → price entry.

paidPlansEnabled.description: CRYP-101 (LAUNCH-FREE). Whether NEW paid subscriptions are available. Non-secret, default true; only false when config says exactly false. Drives the launch-free UI; the server still enforces it in createSubscription, so this is presentation, never the control.

announcement.description: ADMIN-5: the site announcement banner, present (with text + level) ONLY while active, otherwise null. A drafted-but-inactive banner is never published here.

Announcement.description: ADMIN-5: the site announcement banner draft, as returned by getAdminConfig and accepted by saveConfig. `active` is forced false when text is empty.

UserSnapshot.description: ADMIN-5: the READ-ONLY 'view as' snapshot returned by viewUserAsAdmin. Bounded (portfolios/coins/transactions capped) — the `truncated` flags say when there is more. Caps match functions/index.js: VIEW_MAX_PORTFOLIOS=20, VIEW_MAX_COINS=150 (total across portfolios), VIEW_MAX_TX_PER_COIN=50.

hp.description: Honeypot field — must be empty. Any value is silently dropped.

SetSettingsPasswordEnvelope.description: ADMIN-6: set or change the owner-only Settings password.

next.description: The new Settings password (sent over TLS; scrypt-hashed server-side, never stored or echoed). Server floor: min 12 incl. upper+lower+number.

current.description: The current Settings password — required to CHANGE an existing one unless a live unlock is held; ignored on a first-time set.

UnlockSettingsEnvelope.description: ADMIN-6: unlock the Settings screen with the Settings password.

password.description: The Settings password to unlock with.

CompleteSettingsPwResetEnvelope.description: ADMIN-6 PR2: redeem an emailed Settings-password reset token and set the new password.

token.description: The single-use reset token from the emailed link (hex; looked up server-side by its sha256 hash).

next.description: The new Settings password (sent over TLS; scrypt-hashed server-side, never stored or echoed). Server floor: min 12 incl. upper+lower+number.

billing.description: Billing cycle for the scheduled Pro sub. Defaults to monthly.
Billing cycle for the scheduled Premium sub. Defaults to monthly.

question.description: The user's question about their OWN portfolio. Non-blank, trimmed; capped at 500 characters.

answer.description: The validated answer text. Empty string on a fail-closed fallback (fellBack:true).

fellBack.description: True when the fail-closed orchestrator hit the regen cap without a clean+judge-safe candidate — the answer is then the empty safe fallback, never violating text.

downgradeTo.description: Only a premium user may target pro.

AdminEntry.description: One admin in the ADMIN-SEP roster — operational identity only, never a secret.

details.description: Free-text summary of the action. For saveConfig this is a field-level diff (old → new); secret values are never included, only '(changed)'. Bounded server-side to this maxLength (functions/config-diff.js DETAILS_MAX). ROLE-DEPENDENT: Settings is owner-only behind a step-up re-auth, so for a saveConfig entry a non-owner caller receives 'settings changed — details are visible to owners only' instead of the diff (functions/config-diff.js auditDetailsFor).

ip.description: ADMIN-3: source IP the action came from, derived spoof-resistantly from X-Forwarded-For (functions/net-utils.js auditIp). Empty string when no origin is available — e.g. entries written before this field shipped, or under the functions emulator, whose synthetic request carries no address.

result.description: Secrets appear ONLY as boolean set-flags — never the values.

email.description: SMTP-only email — provider-agnostic (any email provider works via SMTP; no provider name is stored). Sends the landing-form signup notification and the Settings-password reset link.

smtpHost.description: SMTP host for outbound email (any provider).

smtpSecure.description: Implicit TLS (true on port 465; STARTTLS on 587 is false).

smtpPassSet.description: ADMIN-6 PR2. Whether an SMTP password is stored — the value is NEVER returned to a client.

requireAdminMfa.description: ADMIN-0. Require a second sign-in factor on EVERY admin callable. Defaults false and is only true when config says exactly true — nothing can satisfy the gate until Identity Platform MFA is enabled. Admin-only: deliberately NOT exposed on the public /api/config. On a save, an omitted key KEEPS the stored value.

paidPlansEnabled.description: CRYP-101 (LAUNCH-FREE). Whether NEW paid subscriptions are available. Default true; only false when config says exactly false. On a save, an omitted key KEEPS the stored value (per-key merge).

generationModel.description: The generation model id (admin config, not a secret) — paste to switch model/provider without a code change.

judgeModel.description: The judge model id (admin config, not a secret).

baseUrl.description: Optional AI provider API base URL (admin config, not a secret). Blank uses the deploy-time default.

monthlyCapCents.description: The app-wide monthly AI spend cap in whole cents (default 5000 = $50). Operational config, NOT a secret — returned as a full number the Settings form can show and edit.

settingsAuth.description: ADMIN-6. Whether a Settings password is set, and when it last changed — the scrypt hash/salt NEVER leave the server.

sentry.description: ADMIN-2. Only whether a DSN is stored — the value is never returned to a client.

data.description: A blank secret field (keys.coingecko, keys.paypalSecret, keys.providerKey, keys.sentryDsn, email.smtpPass) KEEPS the currently-saved value.

providerKey.description: The AI provider API key. keep()-guarded: blank KEEPS the stored value; never echoed back.

generationModel.description: The generation model id (not a secret). KEEP-on-omit: absent preserves the stored value.

judgeModel.description: The judge model id (not a secret). KEEP-on-omit: absent preserves the stored value.

aiBaseUrl.description: Optional AI provider API base URL (not a secret). KEEP-on-omit: absent preserves the stored value.

sentryDsn.description: ADMIN-2 Sentry DSN. keep()-guarded: blank KEEPS the stored value.

aiMonthlyCapCents.description: Plan B PR-E1. The app-wide monthly Wave-B AI spend cap in whole cents (default 5000 = $50). NOT a secret. KEEP-on-omit: an absent value preserves the stored cap; a present value is clamped to a non-negative integer.

email.description: SMTP-only email — provider-agnostic (any provider works via SMTP; no provider name is stored).

smtpHost.description: SMTP host for outbound email (any provider).

smtpSecure.description: Implicit TLS (true on port 465; STARTTLS on 587 is false).

smtpPass.description: ADMIN-6 PR2 SMTP password. keep()-guarded: blank KEEPS the stored value; never echoed back.

requireAdminMfa.description: ADMIN-0. Require a second sign-in factor on EVERY admin callable. Defaults false and is only true when config says exactly true — nothing can satisfy the gate until Identity Platform MFA is enabled. Admin-only: deliberately NOT exposed on the public /api/config. On a save, an omitted key KEEPS the stored value.

paidPlansEnabled.description: CRYP-101 (LAUNCH-FREE). Whether NEW paid subscriptions are available. Default true; only false when config says exactly false. On a save, an omitted key KEEPS the stored value (per-key merge) — the instant maintenance/signups toggles post flags without it and must not reset launch-free mode.

flags.description: A switch omitted from `features` KEEPS its stored value (per-key merge) — it is never re-enabled by omission.

PayPalEvent.description: A PayPal webhook event. Only trusted after signature verification.

DailyStat.description: One UTC day of aggregate growth metrics (statsDaily/{YYYY-MM-DD}). Aggregate only — contains no uid, email or other personal data, which is why the series is retained indefinitely with no erasure path.

date.description: UTC calendar day, YYYY-MM-DD. Also the document id, so ids sort chronologically.

paidUsers.description: pro + premium. Stored explicitly, not derived at read time: it is the churn denominator and a historical snapshot must keep meaning what it meant that day.

canceledSubs.description: Subscriptions cancelled but still holding a paid tier until endDate (forward-looking churn signal).

pastDueSubs.description: Subscriptions with a failed payment, inside the 7-day grace.

signups24h.description: Accounts created in the 24h before this capture, counted from the Auth record creationTime (server-set). A missed scheduled run leaves that window uncounted — the window is fixed, not cumulative.

grossRevenue.description: Monthly-equivalent gross, cycle-true (annual payers at priceYear/12). Rounded to cents.

netRevenue.description: gross - fees. The MRR figure the Overview trends.

limit.description: How many of the most recent days to return. Clamped server-side to 1..400.

capped.description: True when the result filled the requested limit, so older snapshots may exist.

FeatureFlags.description: ADMIN-2 per-feature kill-switches. Each is TRUE unless explicitly false — a missing key or an unreadable config must never read as 'switched off'.

marketData.description: CoinGecko prices/search/coinlist/trending/history. Off = serve cache, make zero upstream calls.

checkout.description: New PayPal subscriptions. Off = createSubscription refuses with failed-precondition.

aiResearch.description: Reserved for the Wave-B AI proxy. No runtime enforcement point exists yet.

JobHealth.description: One scheduled job's heartbeat. `at` is null when the job has NEVER completed — which is a distinct state from healthy, not an absence.

everyMs.description: The job's expected interval; the client flags it late past 2x this.

at.description: Last run that COMPLETED (incl. a deliberate kill-switch skip). null = never.

note.description: e.g. "skipped — marketData off", so unchanged data has a stated reason.

errorAt.description: Last run that threw. Newer than `at` = currently failing.

result.description: Operational status for the admin Overview strip. Contains NO secrets — the Sentry DSN is reported only as a boolean.

paidPlansEnabled.description: CRYP-101 (LAUNCH-FREE). Whether NEW paid subscriptions are available — ON unless config says exactly false. Surfaced on the admin Overview strip.

sentryConfigured.description: True only when a WELL-FORMED DSN is stored — 'configured but malformed' must not read as on.

now.description: Server clock, so the client computes ages without trusting the browser's.
